items: Beat the egg whites until stiff, then slowly add half the sugar.
In another bowl beat the yolks, slowly adding the rest of the sugar, the lemon juice and the potato starch.
Fold the beaten whites into the yolk mixture by hand, adding the nuts as you go.
Bake in a wonder baker on medium-low heat for 1 hour, or in a tube pan at 350°F for 1 hour.
When done, turn the pan upside down and leave it until the cake is cool.
Beat the egg whites until stiff, then add the sugar slowly by hand.
Bake in a wonder baker on low heat for 1 hour, or in an 8x10 inch baking pan in the oven at 350°F for 1 hour.

t: Tips for All Tube Pan Cakes

items: Turn the tube pan upside down and leave it until the cake is cool.
Freeze the cake still upside down in the pan.
Take it out and slice it only when it is completely frozen.
Beat the egg whites until stiff and add half the sugar.
Separately, beat the yolks with the rest of the sugar and the oil.
Combine both mixtures, then add the potato starch and nuts by hand.
Bake in a greased 9x13 inch pan at 350°F for 1 hour.

n: For best results, cut it when frozen.

items: 2 tsp coffee, dissolved in 1 oz boiling water
Beat the egg whites, slowly add the sugar, then add the ground nuts.
Spread in a 16x10 inch baking pan and bake at 350°F for ½ hour.
Meanwhile, mix all the chocolate mixture ingredients together well.
Take the cake out of the oven, pour the chocolate mixture over the top and bake for another 15 minutes.

n: A nut torte with a wine aroma, decorated with [[Nut Brittle]]. Use the [[Easy Chocolate Frosting]] or your favorite chocolate frosting.

items: Beat the whites until stiff, slowly adding ¾ cup of the sugar.
Beat the yolks with the rest of the sugar and fold into the whites.
Add the remaining ingredients and mix only until smooth.
Bake in a 10 inch tube pan at 350°F for 1 hour.
Cut the cake in half through the middle. Spread chocolate frosting on the bottom half and sprinkle with chopped nut brittle.
Put the other half on top and cover the center hole with a piece of cardboard.
Spread chocolate frosting over the whole cake and sprinkle chopped brittle around the sides.

n: Used on the [[Diamond Studs Cake]].

items: A few drops of lemon juice
In a heavy skillet, melt the sugar with the water and lemon juice until it turns liquid and the color of honey.
Spread the nuts on a cookie sheet lined with parchment paper.
Pour the melted sugar thinly over the nuts and let it cool.
Break it with something hard into pieces the size of peas.
Beat the egg whites with half the sugar until stiff.
In another bowl beat the yolks with the rest of the sugar, then slowly add the rest of the ingredients.
Fold the whites into the yolk mixture.
Bake in a tube pan at 350°F for 1 hour.
Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Separately mix all the other ingredients.
Fold that mixture slowly into the whites.
Bake in a 10x14 inch baking pan or a wonder baker at 350°F for 1 hour.
Beat the egg whites with ½ cup of the sugar until stiff.
Beat the yolks with the rest of the sugar, then add the potato starch and lemon juice.
Fold the whites into the yolks.
Bake in a tube pan at 350°F for 1 hour, or in a wonder baker on low-medium heat for 1 hour.

n: Decorate with chocolate mousse cream (page 16) or orange icing.

items: Beat the yolks with ½ cup of the sugar. Add the potato starch, juices and oil.
Beat the whites with the other ½ cup sugar and fold into the yolk mixture.
Bake in a wonder baker on medium-low heat for 1 hour, or in a 9 inch tube pan at 350°F for 1 hour.
Pour ⅔ of the batter into the pan and leave ⅓ in the bowl.
Mix the cocoa with the water or oil and stir it into the batter left in the bowl.
Pour it into the pan and swirl it through with a fork.
Beat the whites, adding 1¼ cups of the sugar, until stiff.
Beat the yolks with the other 1 cup sugar, the oil, potato starch, cocoa and coffee.
Fold the yolk mixture into the whites.
Bake in a 10x16 inch baking pan at 350°F for 1 hour.

n: If you leave out the nuts, add another ½ cup potato starch. Use large bowls.

items: ½ cup walnuts or filberts, ground, optional
Beat the egg yolks until light and creamy, 2 to 3 minutes.
Slowly add 4 tbsp of the sugar and beat a few minutes more.
Add the potato starch, mixing slowly.
Add the lemon juice, banana and nuts (and wine), and mix another minute.
Beat the egg whites until frothy. Add the other 4 tbsp sugar and beat until firm.
Fold the yolk mixture into the whites.
Grease or line a wonder baker or 9 inch tube pan and bake at 325–350°F for about 1 hour.
Beat the whites, slowly adding half the sugar.
Beat the yolks with the rest of the sugar, the potato starch and the lemon juice.
Fold the yolk mixture into the whites, then add the almonds and grated apple.
Bake in a tube pan or 10x14 inch baking pan at 350°F for 1 hour.
Finely grate the potatoes. Add the 6 tbsp sugar, the 6 yolks and the lemon juice and mix well.
Beat the egg whites with the 2 tbsp sugar until stiff, then fold into the potato mixture.
Add the ground nuts and grated chocolate.
Bake in a wonder baker over low heat for 1 hour, or in a 9x13 inch baking pan at 350°F.
1 raw sweet potato, peeled and cubed
Beat the whites with the sugar until stiff.
Blend the yolks, sweet potato, almonds, oil and cocoa in a blender.
Fold the yolk mixture into the stiff whites.
Pour into a 5x8 inch baking pan and bake at 350°F for 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Beat the egg whites with 1 cup of the sugar until stiff and set aside.
Beat the yolks with the other ½ cup sugar, adding the potato starch and cocoa.
Fold the whites into the yolk mixture.
Bake in a tube pan at 350°F for 1 hour.

n: "You'll never believe this cake is Pesachdig."

items: Mix the eggs just until the yolks and whites are combined, not foamy.
Add the rest of the ingredients and mix just until smooth. Do not overmix.
Bake in a 9x13 inch pan at 350°F for 45 to 50 minutes.
Beat the egg whites until stiff, then slowly beat in ¾ cup of the sugar.
Beat the yolks with the rest of the sugar until pale yellow, then add the melted chocolate.
Gently fold into the whites, slowly adding the walnuts, filberts and potato starch. Mix only until smooth.
Pour into a 10 inch tube pan and bake at 350°F for 1 hour.

n: Fill with [[Easy Homemade Apple Jam]], [[Chocolate Mousse Cream]] or ice cream. The outside may be frosted, or simply dusted with [[Homemade Confectioners Sugar]]. Ice cream sandwich cake: bake 2 jelly-roll sheets, fill with the cocoa ice cream, frost with your favorite chocolate cream, freeze and cut into 2 inch squares. Makes 40 squares.

s.h: Cocoa ice cream filling (for the ice cream sandwich cake)

items: Line a cookie sheet (jelly-roll pan) with aluminum foil or parchment paper.
Beat the egg whites at high speed until foamy. Add the sugar and keep beating until stiff peaks form.
Turn the mixer to low, add the yolks and mix until well combined. Fold in the potato starch.
Pour into the pan and bake at 350°F for 20 to 25 minutes, until the top springs back when lightly touched.
Dust a dish towel with potato starch and turn the cake out onto it. Peel off the foil or paper and trim the crusty edges.
While it is hot, carefully roll it up in the towel along the long side.
When cool, unroll, spread with the filling, roll up again and place seam side down.
Beat the egg whites with the sugar until stiff.
In another bowl beat the yolks, slowly adding the oil, until thick.
Fold the whites into the yolk mixture and sift in the cocoa.

n: For Pesach and all year round. If you bake it in a wonder baker, use only ⅔ of this recipe.

items: Beat the egg whites until stiff, slowly adding half the sugar, and set aside.
Beat the yolks with the rest of the sugar until pale yellow.
Slowly fold in the lemon juice, nuts and matzoh meal.
Carefully fold in the whites until well mixed.
Pour into a tube pan and bake at 350°F for 1 hour.
Beat the egg whites until stiff, slowly adding the sugar.
Add the yolks, matzoh meal and lemon juice.
Bake in a wonder baker on medium-low heat for 1 hour.
When done, turn the wonder baker upside down to cool.
Soak the matzohs overnight in the wine and water, turning them until they are soaked through.
Beat the egg whites until stiff, slowly adding half the sugar.
Fold into the yolks, adding the nuts, and mix well.
Line a wonder baker or tube pan with foil. Put in one layer of matzoh.
Spread a little batter on the matzoh and top with a layer of grated apple.
Keep alternating the layers, finishing with batter.
Bake at 350°F for 1 hour. Turn upside down and let it cool a little. Serve warm or cold.
Mix the matzoh meal with the salt and sugar.
Bring the oil and water to a boil and add the matzoh meal mixture.
Beat in the eggs one at a time and mix.
Let it stand 15 to 20 minutes, then shape into rolls with oiled hands.
Bake on a greased cookie sheet at 375°F for about 50 minutes.

n: Great for snacks.

items: Melt the chocolate in a double boiler.
Spread it thinly over the matzoh.
Blend the sugar in a blender on high speed for 1 minute.
Add the potato starch and blend a few seconds more.

n: Variation: spread chocolate mousse cream or [[Easy Homemade Apple Jam]] between 2 ladyfingers to make sandwich cookies. Roll the edges in chopped roasted almonds; they stick to the cream or jam squeezed out from the sides. Or dip the whole sandwich cookie in melted chocolate.

items: Line a square pan with 1 layer of ladyfingers and sprinkle with the wine and water.
While the cream is soft, spread a layer over the ladyfingers and add another layer of ladyfingers.
Repeat to make 3 or 4 layers, ending with ladyfingers, rounded side up.
Refrigerate ½ hour, then freeze, so the cream won't turn watery at room temperature.
Cut into squares, drizzle with melted chocolate and serve.
Beat the egg whites until stiff. Slowly add the sugar and beat until stiff peaks form.
Beat the yolks and mix everything together.
Drop by the spoonful onto cookie sheets lined with parchment paper.

n: Makes about 4 dozen.

items: Beat the egg whites and sugar, then add the rest of the ingredients.
Drop by the teaspoonful onto greased baking sheets and press a walnut half on top of each.
Bake at 350°F for 20 minutes. The centers will be soft.
Mix all the dry ingredients together.
Add the eggs and mix well.
Roll out, cut into pieces and put on a greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 400°F for about 10 minutes, until golden brown.

n: Makes about 4 dozen. Used in the [[No Bake Torte]].

items: In a large bowl, beat the egg whites and salt with a mixer on high speed until soft peaks form.
Slowly add ¼ cup of the sugar and beat until the whites are stiff and glossy.
In a small bowl, beat the yolks with the other ¼ cup sugar (and the vanilla sugar) on medium speed until very thick and pale yellow.
Stir in the potato starch, then fold the yolk mixture into the whites.
Spoon the batter into a piping bag with about a ½ inch tip and pipe 3 inch lengths onto a cookie sheet, 1 inch apart.
Bake at 350°F for about 20 minutes, until lightly browned.
Melt the chocolate with the water in a pot.
In a mixer, cream the sugar and shortening.
Pour the melted chocolate into the creamed shortening and keep mixing for 2 minutes.
Boil the water and sugar, stirring all the time.
Slowly mix in the melted chocolate, stirring slowly until the icing is smooth.
When the icing coats a spoon evenly, beat in the oil.
Dissolve the cocoa and coffee in a few drops of cold water.
In a heavy pot, mix the eggs, sugar and cocoa mixture.
Heat over medium heat until very hot and the sugar is completely dissolved, 6 to 7 minutes. Do not boil.
Add the shortening and mix until it melts.
Take it off the heat and let it cool.

n: When you fill or frost a cake that will be frozen, refrigerate it ½ hour and then freeze it, so the cream won't turn watery when served at room temperature.

items: Melt the chocolate (with the water or wine) in a double boiler until smooth.
Beat the yolks with 2 tbsp sugar.
Turn off the heat and slowly add the yolks to the chocolate. Mix well.
Beat the egg whites until stiff, adding the other 2 tbsp sugar toward the end.
Fold slowly into the chocolate mixture.
Chill in the refrigerator until it firms up enough to spread.

n: Makes 2 layers of frosting for a 10x12 inch cake or a 10 inch round cake.

items: 3 tbsp cocoa, dissolved in 2 tbsp cold water
1 tbsp coffee, dissolved in 2 tbsp cold water
Mix the eggs and sugar in a saucepan and add the dissolved cocoa and coffee.
Heat over a medium flame, stirring constantly, until the sugar is completely dissolved.
When the chocolate has melted, take it off the heat and let it cool.

n: Serve over a slice of cake.

items: Mix the sugar and potato starch in a saucepan.
Slowly stir in the orange juice.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens.
5 lbs ground fish, white or carp
Put all the ingredients except the salt in a mixer and mix for 15 minutes.
Add the salt and mix another 5 minutes.
Divide into 5 loaves and wrap each one in parchment paper.
Put all the ingredients except the fish in a blender and blend until the eggs are foamy.
In a large mixer bowl, add this to the ground fish and mix for 5 minutes.
Divide into 5 loaves and wrap each one in parchment paper.
Refrigerate 1 to 2 hours before cooking, or freeze for later use.

t: Light Gefilte Fish (with hard boiled eggs)

items: Grind all the ingredients except the carrots and raw eggs.
Add the grated carrots and raw eggs and mix until well combined.
Shape into 3 loaves and wrap in foil or parchment paper.
Cook as you would any gefilte fish roll.

n: Makes 8 slices per pound of fish.

items: Mix all the ingredients in a mixer.

t: Cooking Fish for a Crowd (in a disposable roaster)

items: Put the water, onions, carrots and spices in a doubled 11x17 inch roaster over high heat on two burners, until it starts to boil.
Put the fish slices in, turn the heat down to medium and cover loosely.
Cook gently for 1½ hours, then adjust the seasoning.
Let it cool before taking out the slices. Refrigerate.
Put the cleaned fish slices in the roaster and freeze. Thaw before cooking.
Cook the water, onions, carrots and spices in a 6 qt pot for 1 hour.
Strain the liquid and pour it over the fish slices. Cook over high heat on two burners until it starts to boil.
Turn the heat down to medium, cover loosely and boil gently for 1½ hours.
Adjust the seasoning, cool and refrigerate in the roaster, which can serve as the fish container.
To save burner space and keep the fish from scorching, cook it in the oven: put the fish and all the ingredients in the doubled roaster and cover loosely.
Bring to a boil at 500°F, then lower to 400°F and let it boil gently for an hour.
Two roasters of fish can go in at the same time, on two racks.

n: Variation: fill the hollow of each slice with your favorite gefilte fish mixture and carefully put the filled slices into the pot. For a crowd, lay a layer of filled slices on the bottom of the pot of boiling liquid, cover with parchment paper with holes poked in it, and keep adding layers, with parchment paper between every layer.

items: Sprinkle the fish with salt and sugar several hours before cooking, and refrigerate.
Boil the water and add the onions and carrots.
Add the fish slices with the sugar, salt and spices.
Don't take the slices out until they have cooled completely.

n: Serve warm or cold.

items: Clean and wash the fish. Sprinkle with salt and a little sugar and let it stand ½ hour.
Slice the onions into the water and add the carrot and spices.
Add the fish slices and cook for 1½ hours. Let it cool.
Put the fish slices in a dish.
Strain the liquid into a clean pot, keeping at least 3 cups, and bring it to a boil.
In a bowl, mix the potato starch, nuts, 4 tsp sugar and the cold water.
Add it to the boiling fish liquid and cook for 1 minute.

n: Variation: pour a little white wine over the fish just before baking, and bake until all the liquid is absorbed.

items: Mix the oil, paprika and salt.
Grease a 10x16 inch baking pan, put the fish in and spread the oil mixture over it.
Cover with aluminum foil and refrigerate ½ to 1 hour before baking.
Bake at 350°F for 1½ to 2 hours. Uncover for the last ½ hour to brown.
4 tbsp oil, butter or mayonnaise, optional
Peel and slice the potatoes and arrange them in a baking dish.
Sprinkle the potatoes with salt and oil and lay the fish on top.
Bake at 350°F for 1 hour, or broil until done.
Cook in a heavy skillet, covered, over low heat for 1 hour.
Mix all the ingredients except the tomatoes.
Put in a greased foil pan.
Bake at 350°F for 45 minutes, or broil at 450°F for 30 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and bake another 15 minutes.
Shape into patties and fry in hot oil over medium heat, turning to brown both sides.

n: Serves 4–6.

items: Mix all the ingredients and shape into patties.
Fry in oil until well browned on both sides. They can also be broiled.

n: Makes 6–8 portions.

items: Fill an 8 qt pot with 10 cups water and bring to a boil.
Add the chicken and the rest of the ingredients.

n: Serves 8.

items: Put the meat in the 3 qts salted water and bring to a boil.
Add the vegetables and cook over low heat for 2 hours, until the meat is tender.

n: Makes 2 qts. Serve hot with cooked, sliced potatoes.

items: Put all the ingredients together and bring to a boil.
Cook over low heat for 1 to 1½ hours.

n: Serves 8.

items: Peel the vegetables and put everything in a large pot.
Take out the vegetables and blend or mash them with a fork.
Return them to the pot and reheat.

n: Marked "good" by hand in the book. Serve with [[Dumplings I]] or [[Dumplings II]].

items: Sauté the onion in a 4 qt pot.
Add the vegetables cut in chunks and water to cover. Cook for ¾ hour.
Blend the vegetables and pour them back into the water. Simmer another 15 minutes.
When it comes to a boil, add potato dumplings.

n: Optional: add [[Potato Knaidlech (with potato starch)]] or [[Pesachdige Lokshen]], or thicken it: mix ½ cup potato starch with cold water, add to the boiling soup and cook another 5 to 10 minutes.

items: Sauté the vegetables for about 15 minutes.
Add the water and salt and cook on medium heat for 45 minutes.

n: Serves 6.

items: In a 6 qt pot, sauté the onion, parsley root and carrots for 10 minutes.
Add the rest of the ingredients and cook another 1½ hours over medium heat.

n: Family notes written in the book: "x5" and "use ¼ cup measuring cup of batter per blintz".

items: Mix the eggs, salt and potato starch until smooth, then add the water.
Fry thin like blintzes in a little oil or fat.
Roll them up and cut into strips. Serve in soup.
A delicious addition to chicken soup: beat whole eggs and a pinch of salt with a fork until light and fluffy.
Pour into the boiling soup and let it cook 2–3 minutes, until set.
Add the potato starch and salt and mix until smooth.
Drop ½ teaspoonful at a time into boiling soup.

n: For best results, refrigerate 20 minutes or overnight before cooking. The salt amount is written over by hand in the book.

items: ¼ cup club soda or seltzer
Mix the first 5 ingredients well, then add the matzoh meal.
Drop into boiling soup and cook for 20 minutes.

n: Makes 15.

items: 1 lb chicken breast or turkey, ground
Mix all the ingredients very well in a bowl.
Form into small balls and drop into boiling soup.
1 med potato, cooked and mashed (1⅓ cups)
Beat the egg whites and salt with 2 forks or a whisk until foamy.
Mix the yolks, mashed potato and pepper, and add to the beaten whites.
Pour it all at once into boiling soup and cook about 10 minutes on low heat.

n: Makes about 5 portions.

items: 1 cup potatoes, cooked and finely mashed
3–4 cups chicken soup (without chicken or vegetables)
Lightly beat the eggs and salt. Add the potatoes and mix well.
Bring the chicken soup to a boil.
Pour the mixture into the boiling soup all at once.
Cover the pot and let it cook 15–20 minutes, until set.
Drop by tablespoonfuls into boiling soup or water.
Cover and cook for 15 minutes on medium heat.
Mix well and drop by tablespoonfuls into boiling water or soup.
Cook for 15 minutes on medium heat.

n: Makes 10–12 knaidlech. If the mixture is too loose, add more mashed potatoes or starch; if too dry, add another egg.

items: 2 cups potatoes, cooked and finely mashed
Heat the schmaltz or oil in a skillet.
Brown 1 cup of the mashed potatoes until golden, stirring constantly.
Add the rest of the mashed potatoes, the starch, eggs and salt.
Form into balls and cook in soup or salted water.
Mix the matzoh meal with the salt and sugar.
Bring the oil and water to a boil and add the matzoh meal mixture.
Beat in the eggs one at a time and mix. Let it stand 15 to 20 minutes.
With oiled hands, pinch off marble-sized pieces and put them on a greased baking sheet.
Bake in a preheated 400°F oven for 15 minutes.

n: Serve with hot potatoes, in "eier mit zvibel" or chopped liver. Shaking water onto the skins at the end keeps them from getting soggy.

items: Wash and drain the skins and chicken fat.
Simmer in an uncovered pot on medium heat for about 1½–2 hours, until the skin looks crispy.
Raise the heat for 1 minute. Wet your hands and give one good shake of water onto the boiling skins; the schmaltz should sizzle.
Cover and turn off the heat.
Right away, lift out the skins with a slotted spoon, shaking off the extra fat.
Mix the potato starch with the cold water until smooth.
Stir it into the gravy 5–10 minutes before turning off the heat.
1 med chicken, cut into serving pieces
Sauté the onion until clear, about 10–15 minutes.
Add the sliced carrots and lay the chicken pieces over them.
Cook over low heat for 1 hour, adding water only if needed.
1 med chicken, cut into serving pieces
¼ cup light wine (Haute Sauterne or Cream White)
Lay the chicken over the diced onion, skin side down.
Add the jam and wine and cook another 45 minutes, adding water only if needed.
Pour the sauce over the chicken pieces when serving.

n: Serves 8. The sauce can also be used over meat, meatballs or roasts. Written in the book by hand: lemon juice "6 T." and orange juice "1 cup".

items: 2 raw chickens, cut into serving pieces
Put the chicken in a pan or Dutch oven.
Dice the onions and sprinkle them over the chicken.
Squeeze the fruit juices and mix them together, add the water and salt, and pour over the chickens.
Bake at 350°F for 2 hours. On the stove, bring to a boil and lower the heat to simmer for 1½ hours.

n: Serves 6.

items: Clean the chickens and put them in a large pot, skin side down.
Mix the wine and juices, pour over the chickens, cover and marinate in the refrigerator overnight.
Take the chickens out and pour the juice into a container. Set it aside.
Coat the bottom of a Dutch oven with fat or oil and add a layer of sliced onions and sweet potatoes. Put the chicken on top.
Pour half the marinade over the chicken and cook over low heat, checking often and adding water as needed so it doesn't stick.
Mix the rest of the marinade with ½ cup water and pour it over the chicken 10 minutes before the end of cooking.
It can also be baked in the oven the same way, at 350°F for 1½ hours.

n: Made the same way as the [[Marinated Chicken]].

items: The marinade and vegetables from the Marinated Chicken
Cut up the turkey and follow the same steps as the Marinated Chicken.
After the turkey has cooked ½ hour, add the whole peeled sweet potatoes.
Cut the chicken into serving pieces and sprinkle with paprika.
Put it in a covered pan, skin side down, and cook for 1 hour on low heat.
If too much liquid is left in the pan, uncover and cook a little longer on slightly higher heat to reduce it.
Heat the oil in a large skillet and sear the chicken on both sides over high heat until golden.
Lower the heat, add the onions and sauté until clear.
Add the rest of the ingredients and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer 1½ hours until tender, adding liquid if needed.
1 med chicken, cut into serving portions
Brown the chicken in the oil in a heavy pot over high heat.
Add the onions and sauté for one minute over medium heat.
Add the rest of the ingredients and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and cook for 1½ hours.

n: Optional: add cubed liver pieces (chicken, calf or beef) 5 minutes before turning off the heat. If you like, thicken the sauce with 4 tbsp potato starch dissolved in 4 tbsp cold water a few minutes before it's done.

items: 2 tbsp oil or fat, for sautéing
Dash of pepper and paprika, optional
Sauté the diced onion in the oil or fat.
Add the chicken parts, season well and sauté another 5 minutes.
Add water to barely cover and cook for 1 hour.
Mix the chicken ball ingredients well and form into small balls.
Drop the balls into the pot and cook on low heat ½ hour longer, until all the chicken is tender.
Add the salt to the eggs.
Coat each cutlet with potato starch, then dip in the eggs.
Fry on both sides in hot schmaltz or oil until golden and tender.
Coat the fillets with potato starch, dip in beaten egg, then coat with matzoh meal. Fry as above.
Mash 1 cooked potato with 1 beaten egg until it is a smooth batter.
Dip the fillets in the potato batter and fry on both sides.
Mix 2 eggs, 2 tbsp potato starch and 1½ tbsp water until smooth.
Dip the fillets in the mixture and fry on both sides.

n: A make-ahead recipe: the fried chicken is frozen and finished on the day it's needed. Allow 1 chicken for 4 to 6 servings.

items: Matzoh meal or potato starch, to coat the chicken
Oil, enough to cover the frying pan about ¼ inch deep
Cut the chicken into quarters or eighths and coat each piece with matzoh meal or potato starch.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan and fry each piece on medium heat until golden. Don't crowd the pan, so the pieces don't stick together.
As the pieces are done, move them to a large pot and sprinkle with paprika for color. (They won't be cooked through yet.)
When all are fried, cover the pot with a well fitting lid or heavy foil and freeze.
On the day, take the pot out of the freezer, uncover, pour in the orange juice, cover tightly and warm over low heat.
As the chicken thaws, raise the heat a little and cook until it is as tender as you like.
If it needs more liquid to keep from burning, add a little more orange juice, just enough to cover the bottom. Tightly covered, it steams until tender.
Pour the leftover liquid over the chicken before serving, or mix it with the vegetables served on the side.

t: Pan Roasted Chicken for a Simcha or Large Family
n: Conveniently done on top of the stove. It can be frozen after basting: defrost the night before and cook as above. On Yom Tov morning, allow about 3 hours of cooking before the meal. When baking only 2–3 chickens and there's room in the roaster, add 8–10 sliced potatoes about 1–1½ hours before serving.

items: 1 med tomato, peeled or with the inside scooped out
Grate or blend the basting vegetables, add the water and paprika and mix well.
Coat each chicken quarter with the basting.
Spread the 3 sliced onions on the bottom of a 20x13x4 inch disposable aluminum roaster.
Line up the coated quarters so each one leans slightly over the next.
Cover tightly with 2 sheets of heavy duty foil.
Put the pan over 2 burners and cook slowly on low heat for 2½–3 hours, or bake at 400°F for 2–2½ hours.

n: Enough to stuff 1 medium chicken.

items: Mix all the ingredients very well.
Mix the chicken, celery, onion, eggs and mayonnaise (and lemon juice).

n: Serves 8.

items: Sauté the onions in 4 tbsp of the oil or fat until golden.
Mix half the onions with the meat and 2 of the eggs.
Mix the potatoes with the rest of the onions, the other 2 eggs, the other 4 tbsp fat, and salt and pepper as needed.
Put half the potato mixture in a greased baking dish and spread the meat over it.
Top with the rest of the potato mixture and spoon the gravy over.

n: Serves 4. Marked "good" by hand in the book.

items: Sauté the onions in 3 tbsp of the fat until golden.
Add half the onions to the meat, mix with the eggs and spread ½ inch thick over a sheet of parchment paper or foil.
Mix the potatoes with the rest of the onions and fat, and salt and pepper as needed.
Spread the potatoes thinly over the meat.
Roll up like a jelly roll and wrap to keep its shape.
Bake at 350°F for 1½ hours, until done.

n: Serves 6.

items: ½ cup potato starch or matzoh meal
Peel the eggplant and cut into ¼ inch slices. Coat with starch or matzoh meal and fry in hot oil until golden.
Grate or mash the potato and mix all the meat mixture ingredients.
Cover the bottom of a greased 10 inch casserole or Dutch oven with eggplant and put some meat on each slice.
For the sauce, scoop out the tomato pulp (or peel and mash the tomatoes) and mix with the rest of the sauce ingredients.
Spoon the sauce or gravy over the dish.
Bake at 350°F for 1¼ hours, or cook over low heat for 1 hour.
½ cup chicken fat or oil
Blend or grind the chicken, carrots, potatoes and onions.
Add the potato starch and mix well.
Shape into balls, heat the oil in a frying pan and fry on both sides until golden brown.

n: Serves 4 to 6. Optional: leave out the water, add beaten eggs and toss until the eggs are set.

items: Cut the liver into small bite-size pieces.
Sauté the onion in the oil until golden.
Add the liver, cover and cook over low heat for 1 minute only.
Add the salt, pepper and water, cook 1 more minute and serve.

n: Makes 8–10 portions.

items: 2½ lbs chuck kalechl, in one piece
If needed, cut the meat in half horizontally to fit the pot.
Put it in the pot with the onions, seasoning and oil.
Sear for 10 minutes, until browned on all sides.
Add the water and cook on low heat for 2 hours.
Take the meat out of the sauce, cool and refrigerate until firm.
Slice, reheat the slices in their own sauce and serve.

t: Pan-Broiled Minute Steak or Rib Steak

items: 4 slices minute steak or rib steak, thinly sliced
Sprinkle the meat lightly with salt.
Pound it with a mallet to flatten it as much as you can.
Sprinkle the spices over the meat.
Heat the oil in a heavy skillet and fry on high heat until lightly browned.
Turn and fry the other side, 4 minutes in all.

n: Freezes well.

items: Put the tongue in a small pot and cover with water. Boil for 5 minutes and throw away the water.
Cover with fresh water and add the salt, onions and carrots.
Take out the tongue and peel off the skin while it is warm.
Chill in the refrigerator and slice. Serve cold, or reheat in its own sauce.
Warm up the sauce; if it is too strong, add water.
Dissolve the potato starch in the water and add to the sauce.
Bring to a boil and cook slowly for 5 minutes.
Add the sugar and adjust the seasoning.
3 lbs veal breast with bones (ask the butcher to cut a pocket)
1½ lb ground beef, turkey or chicken
Grate or mash the potatoes and mix with the meat, eggs and minced onion.
Stuff the mixture into the veal pocket.
Put the veal in a large pot with the sliced onion, grated carrots and water.
Simmer for 2 hours until tender, or bake loosely covered at 400°F for 2 hours.
2 lbs beef (neck, chuck or shoulder steak), cubed
Brown the meat in the oil or fat.
Lower the heat to medium, add the onions and sauté until golden.
Add the rest of the ingredients and cook over low heat until tender, about 2 hours.
Mix the potato starch with the cold water until smooth and stir it into the sauce 5 minutes before turning off the heat.

n: Makes 4–5 portions.

items: 2 lbs meat (veal chops, single chuck or shoulder steak)
Sauté the onion in the oil until golden brown.
Add the meat, cover and cook over low heat for ½ hour.
Add the water and cook until tender.
3 lbs French roast, brisket, shoulder steak or end steak
¼ cup Cream White or Haute Sauterne wine
Put everything in a covered roaster and bake at 375°F for 3 hours.
To serve, slice and reheat in the sauce.

n: Serves 4–6.

items: ½ lb ground beef or dark turkey
Sauté the onion in the oil or fat until golden.
Add the beef or turkey as is (loose) and sauté another 20 minutes on low heat in a covered pot, stirring now and then.
Add the water, potatoes, salt and paprika.
Cook on medium heat another 30 minutes.

t: The Perfect White and Brown Meat Roll
n: Makes 12 slices, ¾ inch thick.

items: 8 oz chopped beef or dark turkey
Mix all the white mixture ingredients.
Grease foil or parchment paper and spread the chicken mixture on it ½ inch thick. Brush the top with oil.
Mix the brown mixture ingredients well and spread over the white mixture, about ½ inch thick.
Brush the top with oil and roll it up, peeling the foil away as you go.
Wrap it well in foil and twist the ends.
Cover with salted water and cook for 1½ hours, or bake in a covered pan at 350°F for 1½ hours.

n: Makes 4 portions.

items: Boil a pot of water as for real gefilte fish, with sliced carrots, onions, salt and sugar.
Mix all the ingredients well and form into small balls.
Drop them into the boiling water and cook over medium heat for about 30 minutes.

n: Optional: form into long rolls instead of balls. Family notes written in the book: "30 big balls", "½ beef + ½ chicken" for the ground meat, "+ potatoes" with the sliced carrots, and "Do not freeze potatoes & carrots".

items: Mix the first ingredients and refrigerate for 1 hour or more.
In a 12 qt pot, bring the cooking liquid ingredients to a boil.
With wet hands, form the meat mixture into balls and drop them into the boiling water.
Cook for 1½ hours on low heat. Cool and refrigerate.

n: Serves 6.

items: 1 lb beef or ¾ chicken, cut into serving pieces (or bones)
Sauté the onions in the chicken fat or oil on medium heat until golden.
Add the potatoes, salt and the meat or bones, and keep cooking another 35 to 40 minutes.
Add the water, bring to a boil and cook another 30 minutes.
The cholent is now ready to go on the Shabbos blech.

n: Order the chicken neck skin (helzel) from the butcher with the wings attached. Variation: for prettier slices, stuff the neck with 2 hard boiled, peeled eggs too. Slice and serve.

items: Chicken neck skin (helzel), with wings attached
Mix the ground chicken, matzoh meal, potatoes, eggs and grated onion well.
Sew the narrow end of the helzel closed first.
Stuff with the mixture, then sew the other end.
Put it in a Dutch oven with the diced onions, pepper and salt.
Add the water and cook about 1 hour, until done.
½ cup chicken fat or oil
Mix the ingredients, adding enough water to form a dough.
Wrap the dough in aluminum foil and put it into the cooking potato cholent.
Knead all the ingredients into a stiff loaf, adding starch or liquid as needed.
Stuff into a chicken neck skin (helzel) or wrap in foil.
Drop it into the boiling cholent.

n: Variation: drop the potato kugel batter by spoonfuls or cupfuls into the boiling cholent and cook for 1 hour. The result is an excellent potato kugel without frying.

items: Grate the potatoes and drain off the extra liquid. Add the rest of the ingredients.
Cut thin neck pieces from the turkey neck and wings.
Sew one end closed and fill with the kugel mixture from the other end. Sew that end too.
Drop into boiling water for ½ minute, then clean off and remove the feathers.
Cook in your cholent for 1 hour.
Bake the rest of the kugel mixture in a smaller baking pan.
Salt and pepper, to taste, optional
½ lb ground chicken, turkey or beef
Pour half the kugel mixture into a 9 inch baking pan and spread the meat filling over it.
Top with the rest of the kugel mixture.
Bake at 350°F for 1 hour, until done.

n: Variation: the mixture can also be fried as patties.

items: 1 lb ground meat, chicken, turkey or beef
Chicken fat or oil, for frying
Pour into a greased 8x10 inch baking pan.

n: Use your favorite blintz recipe, such as the blintzes in the [[Meat Filled Blintz Pie]].

items: Sauté the onions in the oil until brown.
Add the liver and sauté another 5 to 10 minutes.
Grind with the eggs and salt until smooth.
Fill the blintzes and serve hot.

n: Fills 10–12 blintzes. Use your favorite blintz recipe.

items: Sauté the onion in the oil or fat.
Add the chicken, squash, salt and pepper.
Cook over medium heat about 15 minutes, until the squash is tender, stirring all the time so it doesn't burn.
Mash, fill the blintzes and serve hot.

n: Serves 4. Marked "good" by hand in the book.

items: Beat the eggs. Dissolve the starch in the water and mix with the eggs and salt.
Pour ⅓ cup batter into a hot, greased 10 inch pan, spreading it to coat the bottom evenly.
Fry on both sides until golden. Repeat until all the batter is used.
Mix the meat, eggs and potato.
Grease a casserole or Dutch oven.
Layer the blintzes, meat filling and sliced zucchini, alternating until everything is used.
Bake at 350°F for 1¼ hours, or simmer on the stove for an hour, turning it over before the last 15 minutes.

n: Ideal for reheating meat, chicken or fish, or to spoon over main dishes and side dishes.

items: 4 sprigs celery, diced, or ¼ celery root, grated
Sauté the onion, celery, oil and spices for 15 minutes, until cooked.
Dissolve the starch in the liquid and add to the sauce.

n: Ideal for reheating meat, chicken and fish.

items: Mash or blend the tomatoes and onions (or only the tomato pulp).
Add the oil and spices and simmer over low heat for 30 minutes.
Dissolve the starch in the water and add to the sauce.
Drop by tablespoonfuls into hot oil or chicken fat and deep fry until medium brown.

n: Makes 15–18 knishes.

items: 5 med potatoes, cooked, drained and mashed
½ cup matzoh meal or potato starch
1 cup finely chopped cooked meat, chicken, beef or liver
Sauté the onion in the oil or fat until soft and mix with the potatoes.
Add the eggs, matzoh meal or potato starch, salt and pepper.
Form into balls and press a hollow in the center of each with your thumb.
Fill the hollow with meat and cover with potato mixture.
Flatten slightly into patties and fry on both sides until golden brown.
4 med potatoes, peeled, cooked and cubed
Sauté the onion in the oil until golden.
Add the potatoes and heat for 10 minutes, tossing often.

n: Serves 6.

items: Cook everything in a heavy pot over medium heat for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until cooked.
Put all the ingredients in a 4 qt pot.

n: Variation: sauté an onion in oil until soft and clear, add the mashed potatoes and heat 5–10 minutes on medium-high heat.

items: Heat plenty of oil in a skillet on medium-high heat.
Add the mashed potatoes seasoned with salt, pepper and paprika.
Stir for 10 minutes, until the potatoes are crispy.

n: Serves 4.

items: 2 tbsp matzoh meal or potato starch
Peel the vegetables and grate them coarsely.
Add the eggs, matzoh meal or potato starch, and salt and pepper.

n: Serves 4.

items: Sauté the carrots, oil, sugar and salt over low heat for 30 minutes until tender, stirring now and then.
Dissolve the starch in the water, add to the carrots and stir well.

n: Makes 20 knaidlech.

items: 1 med potato, cooked in salted water and mashed
Mix all the ingredients and refrigerate for 20 minutes.
With slightly wet hands, form knaidlech and drop them into boiling salted water.
Put the knaidlech in a bowl, pour the oil over and toss until coated.
Sprinkle with sugar and nuts and serve.
Cook everything in a pot over low heat for 45 minutes, stirring now and then.

n: Serves 6.

items: Sauté the onion in a small pot until golden. Take it out and set aside.
Add the other ingredients to the oil.
Cover and cook over medium heat, stirring now and then, until the potatoes are cooked, about 30 minutes. Add a few drops of water if needed.
Add the sautéed onions and serve hot.

n: Makes 8 portions. Serve with meat or fish.

items: 3 to 4 med carrots, peeled and coarsely shredded
Sauté the onions in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the carrots and sauté 5 minutes.
Cut the squash in half lengthwise and slice ¼ inch thick.
Add to the carrots and onions, cover and cook over low heat another 15 minutes.

n: Makes 12 balls.

items: Mix the mashed sweet potatoes, orange juice and sugar well.
Shape into 12 balls, about 2 tbsp each.
Roll the balls in chopped pecans.
Put them on a cookie sheet and heat in a 350°F oven for 15 to 20 minutes, until heated through.

n: Serves 8.

items: 8 pineapple slices, ½ inch thick, or 16 apple rings, ¼ inch thick
Butter, oil or fat, for frying
Beat the eggs with a whisk until frothy.
Dissolve the starch in the water. Add everything to the eggs and beat until smooth.
Dip the fruit rings in the batter to coat them completely.
Heat the butter, oil or fat in a heavy skillet and fry over medium heat on both sides until golden.

n: For sweet blintzes, add ¼ cup sugar to the batter. Chicken, meat and liver blintzes are in the Meat section.

items: Beat the eggs with the salt.
Dissolve the potato starch in the water and mix well with the eggs.
Heat 2 tbsp fat in a frying pan.
Pour in ¼ cup batter, spreading it quickly over the bottom of the pan. When golden, turn it over.
Beat the egg white with a fork and add ground walnuts to make a paste.
Add the lemon juice and sugar to taste, and fill the blintzes.
Heat the oil in a frying pan, add the egg whites and cook over medium heat.
While they cook, squeeze the lemon over them and let them curdle.
Drain off all the liquid and sprinkle with sugar.
Fill the blintzes, fry on both sides, sprinkle again with sugar and serve.
Sauté the onion, cabbage and seasoning in the oil on medium heat about 45 minutes, stirring now and then.
Fill the blintzes and reheat. 6 medium kohlrabi, shredded, can be used instead of the cabbage.

n: Use your favorite blintz recipe, like the [[Pesachdige Blintzes]].

items: 3 med potatoes, peeled, cooked and mashed
Sauté the onion in the oil until soft but not brown.
Add to the potatoes with the spices.
Fill each blintz with 3 tbsp of the potato mixture.
Cook the potatoes in salted water, mash and cool.
Shape into balls with a small scoop.
Sauté onions with some salt until light brown.
Add the potato balls and sauté another 10 minutes on low heat, mixing now and then. Serve hot.

n: Optional: add ½ cup coarsely grated apple and/or 2 tbsp chopped nuts. The book says it makes 15; that's changed by hand to 10.

items: 2 tbsp sugar, in the batter (or sprinkle with sugar when done)
Beat the eggs lightly with the water.
Add the rest of the ingredients and mix well.
Fry in hot oil or fat.
½ cup water, apple juice or milk
Break each matzoh into 4 or 5 pieces.
Soak in water, then drain and squeeze.
Mix with the eggs, juice and salt.
Fry on both sides until brown and sprinkle with sugar.
Soak the matzoh in the wine and water, turning often, until soggy.
Make a cake batter: beat the whites until stiff, then add the sugar and yolks.
Dissolve the starch in a little water and add to the batter.
Last, add the drained matzoh torn into bite-size pieces (and the nuts), and carefully mix everything into the batter.
Heat ½ inch of oil in a frying pan and drop in the batter by the tablespoon.
Fry over medium heat on both sides until golden. Serve hot.
⅓ cup oil or chicken fat
Put the matzoh in a large plastic bag and crumble it into farfel-size pieces with a rolling pin.
In a large bowl, beat the eggs, salt and pepper with a fork. Add the crumbled matzoh and mix.
Heat the oil in a skillet and fry for 10 minutes, stirring all the time.
Add 3 to 4 cups boiling water, or as much as it will absorb.
Cover and let it cool for 25 minutes.

n: Makes 4 servings.

items: Crumble the dough with two knives until it looks like farfel.
Brown the farfel in the fat over medium heat until well toasted.
Add as much liquid as it will absorb and simmer 30 minutes, until soft.

n: If the horseradish is too strong, add more apples.

items: Mix the lemon juice with the water.
Add the rest of the ingredients and mix.
Cook the beets and let them cool.
Add the lemon juice, salt and sugar to taste and mix well.

n: Serves 6–8.
Use the [[Pesachdige Mayonnaise]].

items: Peel and cook the potatoes, then drain.
Mix the mayonnaise and lemon juice.
Add the rest of the ingredients and toss well.

n: Serves 8. Written by hand in the book: "x5" next to the cucumbers and onion, and "x4" next to the other ingredients.

items: Chill for several hours and serve.
Tear several leaves into bite-size pieces.
Make lemonade in the salad bowl and marinate the leaves in it for 1–2 hours.

n: Optional: use 1 cup pineapple chunks instead of the apples. Marked "x make" by hand in the book.
Serves 6.

items: 1 eggplant, baked (prick with a knife and cover with foil)
Salt and pepper to taste, optional
Put the oil, eggplant, onion and spices in a heavy pot and cover.
Simmer 45 minutes, then mash with a fork.
Add the chopped eggs. Serve warm or chilled.

n: Makes about 20 scoops.

items: Sauté the onions in plenty of oil or schmaltz until golden.
Mash all the ingredients together, or put them through a meat grinder or food processor.

n: Makes about 15 scoops. Serve hot or cold; for decoration, put each scoop on a lettuce leaf.

items: Matzoh meal or potato starch, as needed, optional
Dip the eggplant slices in the beaten eggs, then in matzoh meal or potato starch.
Fry in hot oil a few minutes on each side and set aside.
Mash everything together, including the fried eggplant, and mix well.

n: Excellent as a dip or spread, or with fresh vegetables. When you refrigerate it, keep the avocado pit in it until serving time so it doesn't turn brown.

items: Chill at least 1 hour, until ready to serve.

n: Serves 30.

items: Mix the eggs, oil, salt and pepper.
Grate the potatoes into the egg mixture and mix well.
Grease the roaster well with shortening and pour in the mixture.
Bake at 450°F for 45 minutes to 1 hour, until slightly golden.
Lower the heat to 350°F and bake another hour, until done.
4 Idaho potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
Heat the oil and arrange a layer of potatoes on the bottom of a frying pan.
Sprinkle salt on each layer; it helps the potatoes stick together. Stack the rest of the layers.
Fry like any potato kugel, about 20 minutes on the first side.
Turn it over and fry the other side, adding more oil to the pan if needed.

n: It can also be pan fried: fry in a covered pan for ½ hour, then turn it over and fry uncovered another 30 minutes.

items: Grate the potatoes and drain off the extra liquid.
Add the rest of the ingredients.
Heat the oil and mix it into the potato mixture.
Pour into a greased baking pan and bake at 350°F until a brown crust forms.
6 medium sweet potatoes, peeled, cooked and mashed
Bake in a 5x8 inch baking pan at 375°F for 1½ hours.

n: Makes 6 servings.

items: Oil or chicken fat, for frying
4 medium potatoes, cut for French fries
6 eggs, beaten with a fork until fluffy
Fry the French fries in oil until done, and drain.
Mix the eggs, salt and potatoes.
Heat 2 tbsp oil or fat in a 10 inch frying pan.
Pour in the potato mixture and fry over medium heat on both sides until golden brown.
Cut into wedges and serve hot.

t: Esther Hamalka Kugel (for second day Pesach)

items: Beat the egg whites until stiff, slowly adding the sugar.
In another bowl mix the yolks, potatoes, walnuts and apple, and fold in the beaten whites.
Fry in a 9 inch frying pan for ½ hour on each side, or bake in an 8x10 inch baking pan at 350°F for 1 hour.
4 tbsp oil or chicken fat, for frying
Heat the oil in a 10 inch frying pan and pour in the mixture.
Cook over medium heat for ½ hour, then turn it over and cook another ½ hour, until golden.
Or bake in an 8x10 inch baking pan at 350°F for 1 hour.

n: Serves 6–8. Use the blintzes from the [[Pesachdige Blintzes]].

items: Mix the sliced apples, sugar and cinnamon.
Put the first blintz in a greased pan and spread a thin layer of apples over it.
Repeat until all the blintzes are stacked, ending with a blintz.
Cover the pan and cook ½ hour on low heat.
Cut into wedges. Serve hot or cold.

n: Serves 6–8. Marked "good" by hand in the book.

items: 6 lg Cortland apples, peeled and diced
Steam the apples in a 2 qt pot on low heat for 15–20 minutes, until tender.
Cool and add the sugar and nuts.
Put the first blintz in a greased 10 inch skillet and spread a thin layer of apple mixture over it.
Repeat until all the blintzes are stacked, ending with a blintz.
Reheat and cut into wedges. It can be served hot or cold.

n: Family notes written in the book: "good fresh", and use the apples "½ grated, ½ sliced".

items: Mix all the ingredients by hand.
Pour into a greased 8x10 inch baking pan.
Bake at 375°F for 1½–2 hours, or fry on low heat in a 5 qt Dutch oven.
Beat the egg whites until stiff. Slowly add the sugar and keep beating until stiff peaks form.
Separately beat the yolks and add the rest of the ingredients.
Bake in an 8x8 inch baking pan at 350°F for 1 hour.
Beat the eggs and sugar well.
Add the oil and beat again.
Mix in the other ingredients and pour into a well greased baking dish.
Bake at 350°F for about 45 minutes, until browned.

n: Serves 10–12.

items: 8 lg Cortland apples, peeled and sliced
Arrange the apple slices on the bottom of a greased 8x10 inch baking pan and sprinkle sugar over them.
Beat the egg whites until stiff, slowly adding the ½ cup sugar.
Add the yolks, potato starch and walnuts and mix together gently.
Pour over the apples and bake at 350°F for 45 minutes.

t: Noodle Kugel with Apple and Nuts
n: Use the noodles from the [[Pesachdige "Lokshen" Kugel]].

items: ¼ cup chicken fat or oil
Heat the oil in a 12 inch frying pan.
Beat the eggs slightly, add the rest of the ingredients and mix well.
Pour into the frying pan and cook over low heat for 20 minutes, until golden.
Turn it over and fry another 10 minutes, until done.
1 lg sour apple, peeled and grated
Beat the 16 eggs, potato starch and water until smooth.
Fry thin blintzes in a greased pan; it makes 16 blintzes.
Roll several blintzes at a time and cut into strips like noodles.
In another bowl mix the kugel ingredients.
Add the noodle strips, mix, and pour into a small wonder baker.
Bake for 45 minutes on medium heat.
Add the rest of the ingredients.
Pour into a greased 5x8 inch pan and bake at 350°F for 1–1½ hours.
Add the salt and pepper to the beaten eggs and scramble the eggs into the sautéed onions.
Cover 1 blintz with ¼ of the egg mixture and top with another blintz.
Repeat 4 times, ending with a blintz.
Reheat in a 7 inch frying pan and cut into wedges.

n: Makes 2 qts.

items: Cook the beets in the water for 45 minutes on medium heat, adding the salt and sugar.
Lightly beat the eggs with a whisk, adding the cold water and lemon juice.
Slowly add 2 cups of the beet liquid to the eggs, mixing all the time.
Pour the egg and beet mixture back into the pot of borscht, whisking hard.
When cool, add the sour cream and mix.

n: Makes 4 servings. Served cold.

items: Cook the potatoes in salted water. Set aside 1 cup of the potato liquid and drain.
Mix the sour cream with ½ cup of the milk and beat with a fork until smooth.
Keep adding the rest of the milk and the saved liquid to the sour cream, beating until smooth.
Pour over the potatoes. Serve cold.

n: Makes about 15 blintzes. Fill with cheese filling, or spread with nuts and sugar, or jam. Serve cold or reheat in a buttered frying pan.

items: Add the sifted potato starch, salt and sugar and beat hard until smooth.
Heat the butter in a 9 inch frying pan and add it to the batter.
When the pan is well heated, pour in ⅓ cup batter, tilting the pan quickly to cover the bottom.
Fry on both sides until golden. Repeat until all the batter is used.
Mix the filling ingredients and fill the blintzes.

n: Cut into squares to serve.

items: Beat the eggs. Add the sifted potato starch, salt and sugar and beat hard until smooth.
Grease a frying pan with butter and pour in enough batter to cover the bottom. Brown lightly on both sides.
Mix the filling ingredients, fill the blintzes and roll them up.
Butter a 10x16 inch baking pan and arrange the cheese blintzes to cover the bottom completely.
Mix the soufflé topping ingredients and pour over the blintzes.
Salt and pepper to taste, optional
Sauté the onion in the oil until golden brown.
Add the squash and sauté 10 more minutes.
Dissolve the starch in the water.
Mix all the ingredients except the butter.
Grease a 9 inch pie plate with the butter, pour in the soufflé and bake at 350°F for 45 minutes.
It can also be cooked on the stove: grease a deep non-stick frying pan or Dutch oven with butter, pour in the soufflé and cook for 1 hour.

n: Serve hot or cold, as a main dish, vegetable dip or sandwich spread.

items: Cook the eggplant and onion in the oil over low heat until tender, 30 to 40 minutes.
Add the salt and let it cool slightly.

n: Serves 5 to 6. It can also be baked at 400°F for 45 minutes.

items: 6 Idaho potatoes, boiled in their skins
Peel the potatoes and shell the eggs.
Heat some of the oil in a deep pan.
Put in 1 layer of sliced potatoes and sprinkle with salt.
Add 1 layer of thinly sliced eggs and sprinkle with salt.
Spread sour cream over the eggs.
Repeat until everything is layered, ending with potatoes.
Dot with the rest of the oil or butter and cook for 30 to 35 minutes.
Mix the dry ingredients with a little milk to make a loose paste.
Stir the paste into the boiling milk until thickened.

n: Can be made only in an oven with a pilot light. It takes 8 to 10 hours to set.

items: Heat the milk for 4 to 5 minutes, but don't let it come to a full boil.
Cool until lukewarm and take off the skin.
Fill a cup halfway with the milk, add 1 tbsp yogurt and mix hard with a fork until all the lumps are gone.
Pour it back into the rest of the milk and mix again very well.
Divide into 5 cups and cover with aluminum foil.
Put a cookie sheet on the bottom of the oven (not the broiler part) and set the yogurt cups on it, as far back as possible.
3 tbsp oil or butter, for frying
Mix all the ingredients well until smooth.
Heat the oil or butter in an 8 inch frying pan.
When hot, add the cheese mixture and fry until the edges are golden, about 30 to 45 minutes.
Beat the egg whites until stiff, slowly adding ½ cup of the sugar.
In another bowl beat the yolks with the other ½ cup sugar and the vanilla sugar.
When fluffy, add the sour cream and beat well.
Carefully fold into the whites and freeze.

n: So the cake doesn't crack, leave it in the oven another hour after turning it off, until it cools.

items: Put the ladyfingers in a plastic bag and crush them very fine with a rolling pin.
Melt the butter in the pan (and spread the crumbs in it, keeping some for the top).
Beat the egg whites with half the sugar until stiff.
Mix all the other ingredients together and slowly stir into the beaten whites. Add the potato starch.
Pour the batter onto the crumbs and sprinkle with the rest of the crumbs.
Bake in an 11x15 inch baking pan at 350°F for 1 hour and 10 minutes.

n: Makes 2 pies. If you have leftover cheese batter, fill a small foil pan for a cheese snack and bake it with the pies.

items: Spread the crust ingredients on the bottom of two 9 inch pie plates and bake at 350°F for 10 minutes.
Blend the filling ingredients in a blender or mixer until smooth.
Divide evenly over the crusts and bake at 350°F for 1 hour.
Mix the topping well, spread over the pies and bake another 10 minutes.

n: Makes 1 qt. Use within 2–3 days.

items: 4 lbs red grapes, with or without seeds
Wash the grapes and blend them in a blender.
Pour into a strainer or colander set over a large bowl. Line the strainer with a coffee filter or cheesecloth for clearer juice.
In the morning, squeeze the grapes to get the rest of the juice.
Refrigerate right away so it doesn't ferment.
Take the grapes off the stems, wash them and blend them whole.
Pour into doubled plastic bags and freeze overnight.
Defrost the night before you need it.
Put the frozen grape juice in a colander and let it drain. Don't squeeze; the juice will be clear.

n: Makes 2 servings. Serve with a slice of [[Sponge Cake]]. Variation: use lemonade instead of the wine and water.

items: Mix all the ingredients in a pot with a rotary beater.
Put on medium heat and keep beating until it boils, about 7 to 10 minutes.

n: Serve the cream chateau over a slice or wedge of cake, in a glass with spoons.

items: Mix the wine and sugar and bring to a boil. Let it cool.
Add the egg yolks and beat together well.
Put it back on the heat and keep beating until smooth.
When it boils, take it off the heat and beat a little longer.

n: Makes 2 qts.

items: Put them in a saucepan with the water, salt and onion and bring to a boil over low heat.
Add the lemon juice and sugar, cook another 15 minutes and adjust the seasoning.
Beat the eggs in a bowl and slowly add the borscht, mixing hard.

n: Ideas for the cooked beets: beet salad (grate, add lemon, sugar and salt to taste); horseradish (grate, add grated horseradish, lemon, sugar and salt to taste); sliced beet salad (4 med beets, sliced, 1 onion, sliced, ½ tsp salt, ½ cup vinegar or lemon juice, ½ cup sugar and 1 cup water).

items: Peel the beets and cut into quarters.
Put them in an 8 qt pot with the 4 qts water and cook gently for 1½ hours.
In a large bowl, beat the eggs. Add the ½ cup water, salt, sugar and lemon juice.
Slowly pour the beet liquid into the eggs, beating hard so it doesn't curdle.

n: The borscht takes 2–3 weeks to ferment.

items: 10 lbs beets, peeled, sliced and cubed
Put the beets in a 6 qt container or pail and fill with the warm water. Add the salt.
Cover with a clean cloth and keep in a very warm place (75° to 80°F) for 3 to 4 days; this is important to start the fermenting.
Keep it in a warm place (70° to 75°F) for two weeks in all.
It will grow a thick layer of mildew that looks like surgical cotton. Before using, strain the borscht to remove it, and take out any soggy beets.
After three weeks, or when it tastes right, refrigerate the borscht.
Taste the borscht for tartness. If too sour, add water; if not sour enough, add lemon juice.
Cook the borscht liquid with the onion for 20 minutes over medium heat, then take out the beets.
Beat the eggs and very slowly add the borscht, beating hard so it doesn't curdle.
Add water to make ½ gallon.
Boil the orange juice, lemon juice and sugar.
Meanwhile, beat the eggs in a mixer.
Add the hot mixture very slowly while beating the eggs.

n: When serving it with a fleishig meal, the halacha is to put a few whole almonds in the almond milk to show it isn't regular milk.

items: Soak the almonds in 1 cup cold water overnight.
Drain and rub off the brown skins.
Blend with the other 1 cup water.
1½ tsp cinnamon or 1 cinnamon stick, optional
Pare and slice the apples and put them in a pot.
Add the water and sugar and bring to a boil.
Add the cinnamon and cook about 20 to 25 minutes.
Dip the apples in the egg whites and oil or wine, then coat with the walnuts and sugar.
2 tbsp cooked beet juice, optional, for color
Cook them in all the other ingredients until tender, about 30 to 45 minutes.

n: Makes 2 cups.

items: 2 lbs (5–6) Yellow Delicious apples, peeled and quartered
Cook the apples and water in a 3 qt pot for about 30 minutes, then cool.
Drain the liquid and blend the apples with the sugars for 30 seconds.
Add the egg and blend another minute.
Blend the starch with a little of the water and juice to make a thin cream.
Bring the rest of the water and juices, the sugar, salt and shortening to a boil and pour over the starch.
Mix and return to the pan to cook for 1 minute. Let it cool slightly.
Add to the beaten yolks, with more sugar or lemon juice if needed.
When cool, fold in the stiffly beaten egg whites.
Pour into dessert dishes and decorate with nuts.
Peel the pineapple, quarter it and remove the core.
Put both through a food processor.

n: Makes 4 to 6 servings.

items: Cut the pineapple in half and scoop the fruit out of the halves.
Remove and discard the core, and cube the rest of the fruit.
Mix the pineapple with the grapes and melon balls.
Pour the Slivovitz and brandy over the fruit.
Let it stand at room temperature for 1 hour, then chill for 3 hours.

n: Serves 6.

items: ½ cup sweet wine, Concord or Muscat
Make a basket: cut wedges from both sides of the top half of the honeydew, leaving a ¾ inch strip between them for a handle. Don't cut the handle; it stays attached to the bottom half.
With a melon baller, scoop balls from the bottom half, hollowing it out, and from the cut-out wedges.
Scoop balls from the cantaloupe halves.
Trim the inside of the handle with a knife.
Put the balls back in the basket, mixing the honeydew and cantaloupe colors.
Pour the wine over the balls and chill well.

n: Optional: add any fruit in season, like sweet cherries, seedless grapes, honeydew or diced kiwi.

items: Squeeze the juice of 1 orange and ½ lemon and add sugar to taste.
Pour over the fruit and refrigerate at least ½ hour.
Beat the egg yolks with the sugar until pale yellow.
Add the melted chocolate and coffee.
Beat the egg whites until stiff and add to the yolk mixture.
1½ cups orange juice, with some fresh orange pieces
Blend all the ingredients in a blender.

n: Tip for freezing Pesach ice cream: so it doesn't settle, freeze the empty ice cream container for 15 minutes before you freeze the ice cream.

items: Beat the egg whites with half the sugar until stiff.
Mix the yolks with the rest of the sugar and add the coffee.
Slowly fold the whites into the yolk mixture.
Spread evenly in an 8x10 inch pan and top with the chopped nuts. Freeze.
3 tsp cocoa or coffee, dissolved in ¼ cup water with 3 tbsp sugar
Beat the egg whites until stiff, slowly adding the sugar.
In a blender, mix the yolks with the rest of the ingredients.
Fold the whites into the yolks.
Spread between 2 layers of jelly roll cake and top with your favorite frosting, or spread on a cake sheet and roll up like a jelly roll.

n: Serves about 8 to 10. For a firmer consistency, add 4 yolks and freeze.

items: Measure the sugar into the mixer bowl.
Peel the apples and grate them into the sugar so they don't turn brown.
Add the egg whites and salt and beat until light and fluffy.
Add the grated chocolate, mixing lightly.

n: White ices: leave out the orange juice and add the yolks. Pineapple ices: use ½ cup pineapple juice instead of the orange juice and leave out the yolks.

items: A few drops of beet juice, for coloring
Beat the egg whites, slowly adding the sugar.
Very slowly add the rest of the ingredients and freeze.
When half frozen, take it out and mix with the K-hook or cookie attachment of the mixer (not egg beaters), or blend in a blender.
If it froze completely first, chop it into pieces, then mix.

n: Good for over-ripe bananas.

items: Mix all the ingredients and freeze in cups.
Any fruit juice, grape juice, lemonade or chocolate milk
For a refreshing treat for kids of all ages, freeze any fruit juice, grape juice, lemonade or chocolate milk in individual cups.
Freeze an orange and cut it into quarters for a healthy treat.
You can also freeze banana slices; they have a very interesting taste.

n: Makes 10–12 servings.

items: Beat the egg whites until stiff, slowly adding the sugar.
Add the rest of the ingredients, mix and freeze.
Mix again by hand after 4–5 hours.
3 tbsp coffee, dissolved in a bit of water, or 2 tbsp melted chocolate
Beat the egg whites and sugar until stiff.
In another bowl, mix the yolks well, slowly adding the oil and flavoring.
Fold the whites slowly into the yolk mixture.

n: Makes 2 cups of potato starch. Shortcut: if moisture and color don't matter, small amounts can be made ½ hour before using, skipping the rinsing and drying.

items: 25 lb Idaho potatoes, peeled and thoroughly rinsed
Grate the potatoes finely in a food processor on high speed, or blend them with as little water as possible.
Put the ground potatoes in a fine-screen flour sifter and let stand 20–30 minutes, collecting the starchy water in a large bowl or disposable pan.
Throw away the ground potatoes; they're no longer useful. The water will be brownish.
Rinse the starch: add cold water ½ inch above it, let it settle 20 minutes, and gently pour off again. Do this 5–6 times until the starch looks pure white.
Leave the starch in the bowl to dry about 2–3 hours.
Spread it on clean white paper on a table and let it dry completely again, about 12 hours or overnight.
Sift the starch for a fluffy texture.
Mix the sugar and cocoa in a saucepan.
Mix in the water and cook until smooth and thick, stirring about 5 minutes.
Keep in a covered bottle in the refrigerator.
Peel the grapefruits and oranges and remove the membranes.
Cut into small pieces and put into a 3 qt pot with the sugar.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 45 minutes.
Stir with a wooden spoon, raise the heat and boil uncovered 20 minutes longer, stirring often so it doesn't burn.
Take off the heat, cool and put in glass jars. Cover and refrigerate until needed.

n: Makes 12 oz apple jam. For a spreading consistency, mix in a little hot water (about ¼ cup) until it's right. Used in [[Chicken 'n' Wine]] and the [[Pesach Jelly Roll]].

items: Simmer all the ingredients on medium to low heat for 45 minutes, stirring often.

n: Makes 1 pint.

items: Very slowly add the oil, beating until it gets thick.
Add the salt and lemon juice and beat a little longer.
Mix it with the raw yolk, sugar and salt with a fork.
Mix in a little oil until it gets hard and thick.
Add a little vinegar, mixing all the time.
Keep adding oil and vinegar in turns while mixing, until it's the right thickness for mayonnaise.
